solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resume it after a fashion when retired

indicators.note: done after a fashion means done in a rough, approximate way, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A pensioner is advised to dust off the old CV and job-hunt again after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resume' looks like the French CV, but it is simply the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor or official who has left office but keeps an honorary title, so it means retired.

clue.text: Heavenly girl occupied by study lacking bit of dash

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside, so the girl's name holds the other piece
lacking means without, so a letter goes

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dreamy girl is absorbed in her studies but short on verve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' suggests verve, but only its opening letter is wanted, removed from the word for study.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and otherworldly, as if belonging to the sky or heaven, so it matches heavenly.

clue.text: Best to arrest main suspect for murder

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so the first piece holds the second
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Top detectives are told to bring in the chief suspect in a murder case.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate someone is a euphemism for killing them, so the verb stands for murder.

clue.text: Children's publication

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an edition of a magazine or paper

explanation.surface: A magazine aimed at young readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s joins the two meanings, making them look like one title for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language and also an edition of a periodical.

clue.text: Social climber finds posh prostitute having second thoughts

indicators.note: having means holding, so the prostitute holds the afterthought inside

parts.note: a postscript is a second thought added to a letter

explanation.surface: An ambitious arriviste discovers an upmarket call girl wavering about her client.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in rank and behaves arrogantly, much like a social climber.

clue.text: A passage from Camus edified and entertained

indicators.note: a passage is an excerpt lifted out of a longer text, so the letters are found running inside the words

parts.note: found spanning the end of the writer's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A reader finds an extract from the French existentialist both uplifting and diverting.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to have been diverted or made to smile, a straightforward synonym of entertained in its past sense.

clue.text: Married sailor follows woman to Malta at the end of this novel

indicators.note: follows puts the sailor behind the woman in the answer

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
M is Malta's international vehicle code

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A wedded seaman trails his lady to Malta as this story closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Men at Arms is the first novel of Evelyn Waugh's Sword of Honour trilogy.
explanation.definitionFit: Men at Arms is a 1952 Evelyn Waugh novel, so the phrase names a work of fiction.

clue.text: Heads of Sociology think Oxford represents exceptional value

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Sociology dons reckon an Oxford degree is outstanding value for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To set great store by something is to prize it, so store can mean worth or value placed on a thing.

clue.text: Force of river splitting Dutch ship

indicators.note: splitting means coming between, so the river goes inside

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: The current of a river breaks a Dutch vessel in two.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a frequent crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion by threats or force, as in a confession signed under duress.

clue.text: A lawyer receives money from him to make a false statement before end of session in court

definitions.text: A lawyer receives money from him

indicators.note: in places the statement and letter inside the court

parts.note: CT is an abbreviation for court
a lie is a false statement

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A barrister is paid by someone who goes on to lie in the closing stage of a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is the person who engages and pays a lawyer for professional services.

clue.text: Hard when accepting the Italian's praises

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: as can mean while or when
il is the Italian masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A tough critic grudgingly applauds an Italian's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to acclaim or salute them enthusiastically, so hails works as a verb meaning praises.

clue.text: Brilliance of poet talking about Lepanto's opening

indicators.note: talking means we go by how the built word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: the poet Stephen Spender with the first letter of Lepanto placed inside, then said out loud

explanation.surface: A poet holds forth on the start of the famous sea battle of Lepanto, a dazzling subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender was a twentieth-century English poet; 'about' puts L inside his name, and SP(L)ENDER is pronounced just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or dazzling grandeur, the same idea as brilliance in its sense of impressive display.

clue.text: Repeat it with hesitation after soldiers come to value missing king

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the following item is taken away
after places what comes before it in the clue later in the answer than the soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone says something again, haltingly, after soldiers arrive to assess it without the king.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE loses its R to leave ATE; 'come to' simply links the wordplay to that final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say again, often for emphasis, so it is a direct synonym of the verb repeat.

clue.text: Emphasise getting rid of second lock

indicators.note: getting rid of means discarding, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Instructions to underline the point about removing a second lock, perhaps of a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock or curl of hair, so the noun matches lock in its hair sense.

clue.text: In anticipation of profits after a time

indicators.note: after tells us the profits are placed following the article

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An investor waits in hope of making money after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a time' reads as one phrase, but 'after' places the profits behind A, with time supplying the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To save against a rainy day is to prepare for it, so against can mean in preparation or anticipation of.

clue.text: Students receiving books on old city of ill repute

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the students hold the rest

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Undergraduates are sent books about an ancient city with a bad reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, the same as having an ill reputation.

clue.text: Bird disease

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a songbird with a speckled breast
second meaning: a fungal infection, candidiasis

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a common speckled songbird and a yeast infection of the mouth or genitals.

clue.text: Collect carbon inside new German apparatus for waste removal

indicators.note: inside places carbon within the verb for collect

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather carbon in some new German machine for disposing of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New German' looks like a description of the apparatus, but each word supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger can be a device or creature that clears away refuse, such as an exhaust-clearing system in an engine.

clue.text: Old king spotted piece of lovage in salad dish

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: a word for spotted wraps round the herb's letter, which sits within it
a piece of a word here is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch notices a sprig of herb in his side salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage in dressing, served as a side dish.

clue.text: Held in small enclosure with sheep

parts.note: a pen is a small enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Livestock kept in a small fold alongside a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Pent up describes feelings or creatures confined and restrained, so it matches held in as an adjectival phrase.

clue.text: Union leader moved out of fashionable part of London

indicators.note: moved out of means departed from, so the letter leaves the word
the leader of a word is the one at its front, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trade union boss relocated from a trendy London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is a district in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is an area of Tower Hamlets in east London, so it is one part of the capital.

clue.text: Secret police tapes go fuzzy

indicators.note: fuzzy means blurred and indistinct, so the letters are jumbled out of focus

parts.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Surveillance recordings by the secret police turn out blurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police force of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Appropriate beginning to article on English

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the pieces follow one another

parts.note: the germ of an idea is its beginning
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A suitable opening for a piece of writing about the English language.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant to the matter in hand, so it works as an adjective meaning appropriate or pertinent.

clue.text: Diverse area seen during unfamiliar drive

indicators.note: something seen during another is within it
unfamiliar means strange and not as we know it, so the letters appear in a new order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A mixed landscape is passed on a trip along unknown roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Varied means showing variety or many different kinds, which is what diverse means.

clue.text: Change seen in man after wife leaves

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so this letter departs from the name

parts.note: any man's name will do; here Walter
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband becomes a different person once his wife walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or make it different, a plain synonym for the verb change.

clue.text: Characteristic of conveyance after poles are removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so letters are dropped

parts.note: transit is carrying from place to place

explanation.surface: A feature of a vehicle once its tent poles have been taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature, so the noun means characteristic.

clue.text: Soldier on exercises runs hard

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A soldier on drill is put through punishing workouts and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' looks like a soldier doing something, but it is the phrasal verb meaning keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, exactly what the idiom soldier on means.

clue.text: A number of them almost raised over a grand

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, from bottom to top
over here means spread across and covering, so it straddles the next letters
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a means one, I in Roman numerals
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Some of them nearly lifted more than a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: THEM loses its M; THE read upwards gives EHT, which goes round I and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a whole number, so it is simply a number; the article A belongs to the definition.

clue.text: Artist volunteers to follow Naomi's distracted lover

indicators.note: to follow puts the artist and volunteers after the name in the answer
distracted means confused and scattered, so the name's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A painter and some volunteers trail after Naomi's lovesick, absent-minded boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman with whom one is in love, so it names a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Leave to work with Latvia's top dramatist

parts.note: a machine that goes is working

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone departs to collaborate with Latvia's leading playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian-Ukrainian author of The Government Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Gogol wrote the comic play The Government Inspector, so he is a dramatist as well as a novelist.

clue.text: Abhor extremely divisive experiment

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a highly controversial trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely divisive' reads as very divisive, but extremely takes only its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to hate intensely, which is what abhor means as a verb.

clue.text: Condemned housing

parts.note: surface reading: buildings declared unfit to live in
setter's reading: the cells where prisoners sentenced to execution are kept

explanation.walkthrough: Condemned buildings are slated for demolition; read as people condemned to die, the housing is the prison block they wait in.
explanation.definitionFit: Death row is the part of a prison where inmates under sentence of death are held.
